title: 10 Medieval Torture Devices
summary: Josh and Chuck tour ten medieval torture devices, noting the Middle Ages' violence, and playfully check which device names double as heavy metal band names (Brazen Bull, Thumb Screws, Pilly Wink, Rack, Wheel, Steak, Pillory, Iron Maiden, Scavenger's Daughter, Breast Ripper, Pear of Anguish). They cover how each device worked, its grim uses, and the Iron Maiden of Nuremberg, plus stoning and the pillory's public humiliation. The episode closes with a listener mail about a witness-protection-style house full of home automation gadgets.

segments.title: Opening and warning
segments.summary: Hosts warn listeners the episode is gruesome and introduce the Medieval period, its violence, short life expectancy, and the Church's role after Rome fell.

segments.title: Brazen Bull
segments.summary: The Brazen Bull, a brass bull used to roast victims inside by fire, invented by Perillus for the tyrant Phalaris; the hosts note it is also a metal band name.

segments.title: Thumb screws and pilly wink
segments.summary: Thumb screws crush the thumbs without intending to kill; a finger version called the pilly wink is described, with Tam Dalyell mentioned as a user.

segments.title: The rack and the wheel
segments.summary: The rack stretches the body by pulling the limbs apart; the wheel ties victims to a spoked wheel, used for pendulum swings or rolling down hills. Torquemada's preferred device is mentioned.

segments.title: The steak
segments.summary: Victims were tied to a stake and burned, often taking about thirty minutes to two hours to lose consciousness; in the Netherlands the tongue was sometimes clamped between hot plates; strangling before burning was a mercy for confessed heretics.

segments.title: The pillory and public shaming
segments.summary: The pillory held people in public for humiliation, where crowds could pelt them with rotten food or beat them, sometimes to death. The hosts also discuss stoning as a modern execution method and a 1990s paper on execution pain.

segments.title: Iron Maiden of Nuremberg
segments.summary: The Iron Maiden, a spiked sarcophagus-like device that pierced the victim's organs, with a Nuremberg example; a Maiden was also found at Uday Hussein's Ministry of Sports in Iraq. The hosts mention the Iron Maiden beer.

segments.title: Scavenger's Daughter
segments.summary: The Scavenger's Daughter compressed the body into a crouched position with an arch-shaped screw, named for inventor Skevington; an example is displayed at the Tower of London.

segments.title: Breast ripper and pear of anguish
segments.summary: The breast ripper was a clawed device used mainly on women to mark and shame them; the pear of anguish, a pear-shaped expanding device, was used on women and homosexual men. The hosts discuss gendered torture and the end of such practices.

segments.title: London Dungeon and closing torture remarks
segments.summary: The hosts mention the London Dungeon attraction and the search tip for medieval torture devices.

segments.title: Listener mail: witness protection house
segments.summary: Matthew from Cook describes his friend Michael's aunt's house, a former witness protection property with many hand-built automation switches, backup power, and a wind turbine.
